findings.title: Life and death held in an intermediate state
findings.claim: The paired negations make an intermediate condition perceptible: death is withheld while ordinary living is withheld as well, so the focus can describe persistence stripped of flourishing rather than a logical wording accident.
findings.mechanism: The separate imperfect predicates for dying and living are coordinated under two negative particles. Each focus root supplies the independent pole that keeps the other live, and the later named life in 87:16 gives the life branch an evaluative context.
findings.reader_payoff: The paradox becomes a held interval whose lack of life is meaningful precisely because death has also been held back.
findings.containment: The plain statement remains the focus's primary death/life negation; this finding names the relational effect of the pair and does not redefine either verb or assert a general doctrine.

epistemic.reason: The focus morphology and exact same-surah 87:16 life occurrence directly ground the bounded cross-root relation.

findings.title: Preservation without clemency

findings.containment: This is a surprising anti-clemency analogy anchored in the paired focus verbs and 87:17; it does not claim that the local death or life verbs lexically mean pardon.
